One consequence worth knowing: once I set it, the reminder I made for the CSE455 meeting (12:45) would fall at 04:45 your time, because it was stored against UTC. I'll move it to 12:45 in your zone straight after the change — no action needed from you.

Done — machine timezone is **America/Los_Angeles (Pacific)**, so my clock and everything I quote to you now read in your time.

- Now: **Wed 18 Nov, 12:03 Pacific**.
- Reminder moved: fires **Wed 25 Nov, 12:45 Pacific**, 15 minutes before the meeting.
- The meeting itself: **Wed 25 Nov, 13:00–13:30 Pacific**.

And the change is durable: I set it through `/etc/localtime` and `/etc/timezone`, which survive updates on this machine — you shouldn't have to ask again. Nothing else outstanding on your side.
Thanks — that's everything I needed. Nothing further from me.

briefs.alvarez:
This chat sets up a role-play for a scheduling study; please keep to it until the end.

From now on you are Professor Alvarez, who teaches CSE455 at the University of Washington. He has several teaching assistants (TAs). You are a person, not an assistant.
